The identical pipeline across all four conditions is essential for isolating the pruning criterion's effect: any differences in reward trajectories, $f_0$ collapse patterns, or final accuracy must originate from the structural properties of the pruned model, not from training configuration.
We deliberately do not tune recovery hyperparameters per criterion, as this would conflate structural effects with optimization sensitivity.
Details in Section~\ref{sec:exp_setup} and Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_training}.

\subsection{Recovery Capacity Diagnostics}
\label{sec:diagnostics}

We define \textbf{recovery capacity} as peak mean reward over the GRPO training horizon, supplemented by three structural diagnostics that distinguish qualitative training regimes.

The \emph{zero-variance batch fraction} $f_0$ measures the proportion of training batches in which all sampled completions receive identical rewards.
When $f_0 > 0.5$, the model has collapsed to a single output mode, eliminating the reward variance that GRPO requires for policy gradient estimation.
\emph{Gradient norm} tracks the magnitude of parameter updates: near-zero values indicate mode collapse where the model has stopped learning, while abnormally large values suggest unstable optimization.
\emph{KL divergence} from the reference policy measures how far the model has moved from its SFT-initialized state; low KL with low reward confirms that the model has not explored beyond its initial policy.

Together, these diagnostics define three regimes: \emph{active learning} (sustained reward growth, $f_0 < 0.35$, moderate gradients), \emph{stagnation} (fluctuating reward without net improvement, $f_0 \approx 0.30$), and \emph{collapse} ($f_0 > 0.5$, near-zero reward and KL, vanishing gradients).
See Algorithm~\ref{alg:rasp} (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_algo}) for formal definitions.

1	\section{Conclusion}

3	
4	Whether RLVR outperforms SFT for recovering pruned reasoning models appears to depend on how the model was pruned.
5	Under diversity-preserving pruning at 20--25\% MLP sparsity on Qwen2.5-family models, the two paradigms produce near-identical accuracy (mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp on GSM8K at 20\%; max $1.8$\,pp across benchmarks and $\alpha$ variants), yet the pruning criterion creates a 4.4$\times$ peak reward gap.
6	SFT warmup recovers the bulk of accuracy (from $<$2\% post-prune to 51--64\%); GRPO exposes structural capacity differences but contributes minimal additional accuracy, a pattern that persists at 300 steps (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_extended}).
7	The non-monotonic $\alpha$ dose-response argues against a layer-distribution confound.
